description: One machine-readable inventory of every governance guard and gate check that can refuse a governed verb or fail a gate. Documentation and measurement only: no guard's behaviour changes. Tiers are proposals (direction only, ADR 0021): reduced gates switch on only after this registry is reviewed and tier classification and affected-test selection are validated against full runs.
tier_semantics: T0, T1 and T2 are PROPOSED review classifications, not enforcement thresholds. Under ADR 0021 no enforcement changes until this registry is reviewed and tier classification and affected-test selection are validated against full runs; until then every guard runs for every ticket. The proposal: a tier is the lowest ticket tier at which the guard would run (T0 every ticket, T1 for T1 and T2 tickets, T2 only for policy, trust, identity, upgrade, release and ADR tickets). Ownership, provenance and integration-safety guards stay enforced at every tier: they are marked always_enforced and classified T0.
ownership: Classification changes (tier, always_enforced, editions, proposed merges, retirement) need human-admin review through a governed ticket that cites ADR 0021. Adding a guard means adding its entry, with a guard:<id> marker or an anchor, in the same change. An intentional rewording of a refusal message must update that site's registry anchor in the same change: the completeness check failing on a stale anchor is the intended signal, not something to silence. Coverage baselines are never refreshed to accommodate markers; a marker that makes the ratchet report new uncovered code is moved or registered by anchor instead.

measurement.source: remote gate of 2026-11-05 on tree 61bf80c0 (COORD-871..888 stack; n22 and n24 full suites with coverage and dual-release run in parallel on one host)
measurement.note: Only the gate-stage figures from this run count as measured. Every other cost is recorded as unknown (wall_time null, cost_status unknown); none is an estimate. Per-verb frequency is structural (from the code path), not measured.

covered: refusal-call: a fail()/die()/refuse()/throw new X() call in coord/engine/scripts/** production code whose call text (up to 6 lines) says refuse/refused/refusing/refusal or "Review-plan blockers"
refusal-text: a string literal with that wording outside a refusal call (message builders such as formatTreeMutationSafetyHazard)

blocker-code: a `code: "<name>"` blocker pushed by the start, submit and review-plan readiness collectors (coord/engine/scripts/gates/**, review-plan-readiness.js, decomposition-proof-gate.js, gate-plan.js, governance-validation.js)
deny-decision: a `decision: "deny"` result from a runtime-authority, auto-mode or containment policy

wrapper: a shared guard helper defined as assert<Name>, collect<Name>Issues/Blockers or format/build<Name>Refusal (assertRegisteredBoundOwner, assertProductionLocForCloseout, the review-plan blocker collectors, seal and drift assertions)
stage: dynamically dispatched gate stages — release/check-public-release.sh CHECKS, the test-runner overallPass terms, arch-checks CHECKS and verify-upgrade-bridge.sh steps

not_covered.surface: Refusals without refusal wording outside a guard wrapper
not_covered.reason: A fail()/throw whose message neither says refuse/refused nor sits in an assert*/collect*Issues wrapper is invisible to the wording scan (for example argument validation such as "<verb> requires <ticket-id>", and the co-located-writer message). The registry lists the known ones with marker:true locations, so their markers are enforced in that direction only; a new unworded refusal is not detected.

not_covered.surface: Enterprise-only guards in a Community cut
not_covered.reason: The Community cut strips the Enterprise-only subtree, so its check does not see these entries; the donor and the Enterprise cut check them. Files there are named with the @enterprise/ prefix because the Community open-core scan forbids the subtree's path in shipped files.
The Enterprise adapter authorization policy and the conformance-bundle and rehash verifiers return result codes rather than refusing a verb; they are scanned but contain no refusal-worded site today.
Signature, attestation and conformance verifiers (journal-signing.js, conformance-attestation.js) return result codes rather than refusing a verb; their callers' refusals are scanned.
cli.js and governance-mcp.js route verbs to handlers; the scan covers the guard sites those handlers reach, not the routing tables themselves.
Shims are thin re-exports of engine modules (coord/engine/shim-registry.json); the engine targets are scanned.
Commands recorded with gov add-repo-gate are adopter-defined; only the repo-gate record guard is in scope.

not_covered.surface: Release scripts other than the listed stages
not_covered.reason: release/build-public-release.sh, publish-*.sh, scan-*.sh and the release/*.js checkers are reached through check-public-release.sh stages; their internal fail paths are not scanned individually.
The 2026-11-05 legacy-entrypoint script lived in a scratch kit, not the repository; the in-repo equivalent is verify-upgrade-bridge.sh step 6.
*.test.js files are excluded; they prove guards, they are not guards.

guards.title: Legacy entrypoints load
guards.intent: Every registered shim at a legacy coord/scripts path loads and returns its engine module.

cost.note: Not measured (the 2026-11-05 kit ran it after the timed stages).

guards.remedy: register the missing shim in coord/engine/shim-registry.json
guards.retirement_criteria: Retire only when ALL hold, recorded in the ticket closeout (COORD-960): (1) Concord 0.2.0 (COORD-912) has shipped with the runtime deprecation warning on every removable shim (COORD-991); (2) the removable shims are retired in the 0.3.0 batches, so coord/engine/shim-registry.json has no kind=removable entry; (3) the COORD-589 window closure is recorded (COORD-868 or a successor record). Until then the guard stays, and its adopter risk is covered in-suite by coord/engine/scripts/legacy-entrypoints.test.js (every registered JS shim loads and returns its engine module, with a negative control). The permanent stable-entrypoint shims (14) are not removed by this retirement.

guards.title: Upgrade bridge
guards.intent: An adopter on the last release can upgrade to the new cut and the result verifies end to end, idempotently.

cost.note: Not measured (the 2026-11-05 kit ran it after the timed stages).

guards.remedy: fix the failing step; re-run release/verify-upgrade-bridge.sh <old> <new> --keep
guards.retirement_criteria: Retire only when ALL hold, recorded in the ticket closeout (COORD-961): (1) v0.1.16 is out of support, evidenced by the 0.2.0 release (COORD-912) having shipped with a real adopter upgrade canary, so no supported adopter remains on v0.1.16; (2) the v0.1.16 bridge rollback regression is kept in-suite (coord/engine/scripts/coord-upgrade.test.js: the COORD-885 new-directory fixture and the COORD-961 rollback test, with the COORD-886 post-apply read test) so must_still_cover stays covered after removal. Until then the guard stays. As of 2026-11-14 neither holds: COORD-912 is todo and the package is still 0.1.16.

throw new Error(`refusing shard cleanup without preserved normalized coverage for shard ${worker.id}`);

throw new Error(`refusing to remove shard ${worker.id} manifest with its worker directories`);

throw new Error(`refusing shard cleanup with unexpected census ${label} path for shard ${workerId}`);

guards.title: Multi-PR closeout refuses duplicate or no-PR references
guards.intent: A multi-PR closeout requires live verified PR references and refuses duplicate PR refs, so attribution is never ambiguous.

anchors.text: if (new Set(keys).size !== keys.length) return fail(`Ticket ${args.ticketId} records duplicate PR refs; refusing ambiguous multi-PR attribution.`);

guards.remedy: record each distinct PR once with gov set-pr, then re-run the closeout
